question.problem:
Consider two sets of $36$ paired observations ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{36},$ and ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{36}.$ You are given that

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{xx}=72,\,{S}_{yy}=36,\,{S}_{xy}=54.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, ${\sigma }_{x}^{2}=$
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
Given a set of $n$ paired observations ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ and ${y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n},$ the variance of ${x}_{i}$ can be calculated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{x}^{2} & =\frac{{S}_{xx}}{n},\end{aligned}
$$

where ${S}_{xx}$ is the sum of squared deviations from the mean for the data ${x}_{i}.$

We are given that ${S}_{xx}=72.$ Substituting the given statistic in the above formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{x}^{2} & =\frac{72}{36} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
